hero.title: A practical guide to building agents
hero.en: Agents independently accomplish tasks on a user's behalf by managing workflow execution, using tools, and operating within guardrails.
hero.zh: Agent 不是套了聊天界面的 LLM，而是在明确护栏内管理工作流、调用工具并代表用户完成任务的系统。

summary.lead: 正确结论：构建 Agent 的起点不是追求最大自治或复杂多 Agent 架构，而是先确认场景确实需要处理模糊判断、非结构化信息或脆弱规则，再用模型、工具、指令、评估、护栏和人工介入机制逐步扩展。

keyPoints.label: 核心判断
keyPoints.text: Agent 的边界在于是否由 LLM 管理工作流执行并动态选择工具。

keyPoints.label: 适用条件
keyPoints.text: 复杂决策、规则难维护、非结构化数据依赖，是比“能不能接入 LLM”更重要的判断标准。

keyPoints.label: 落地路线
keyPoints.text: 先单 Agent、强模型和 eval 建基线，再按复杂度演进到多 Agent、分层护栏和人工介入。

cards.title: 先定义边界
cards.body: 聊天机器人、单轮 LLM 和分类器不是 Agent；Agent 必须能推进工作流。

cards.title: 再判断场景
cards.body: 只有传统确定性方法不够用时，Agent 才更可能创造价值。

cards.title: 打牢三件套
cards.body: 模型负责推理，工具负责行动，指令负责约束和执行方式。

cards.title: 默认从简单开始
cards.body: 单 Agent 加工具循环更容易评估和维护，拆分多 Agent 应有明确触发条件。

cards.title: 护栏进入主路径
cards.body: 相关性、安全、PII、工具风险、输出校验和人工介入共同决定生产可靠性。

cards.title: 以真实反馈迭代
cards.body: 成功部署不是一次性架构设计，而是小步验证、持续 eval 和逐步扩展。

sections.title: Agent 的边界：工作流执行权

rows.en: Agents are systems that independently accomplish tasks on your behalf.
rows.zh: Agent 是能够代表用户独立完成任务的系统。

rows.en: Applications that integrate LLMs but do not use them to control workflow execution are not agents.
rows.zh: 仅集成 LLM、但不让 LLM 控制工作流执行的应用不应被称为 Agent。

rows.en: The agent can halt execution and transfer control back to the user in case of failure.
rows.zh: 可靠 Agent 还必须能在失败时停止执行，并把控制权交还给用户。

sections.title: 什么时候值得构建 Agent

rows.en: Agents are uniquely suited to workflows where deterministic and rule-based approaches fall short.
rows.zh: Agent 适合传统确定性方法或规则系统难以覆盖的工作流。

rows.en: Prioritize complex decision-making, difficult-to-maintain rules, and heavy reliance on unstructured data.
rows.zh: 优先选择复杂决策、规则难维护、以及高度依赖非结构化数据的场景。

rows.en: Otherwise, a deterministic solution may suffice.
rows.zh: 如果用例不满足这些条件，确定性方案可能已经足够。

sections.title: 模型、工具、指令构成最小系统

rows.en: An agent consists of three core components: Model, Tools, and Instructions.
rows.zh: Agent 的基础结构由模型、工具和指令三部分组成。

rows.en: The model powers reasoning and decision-making; tools let the agent take action.
rows.zh: 模型负责推理和决策，工具让 Agent 能与外部系统交互并采取行动。

rows.en: Instructions define explicit guidelines and guardrails for how the agent behaves.
rows.zh: 指令定义 Agent 的行为准则、步骤和护栏，减少解释空间。

rows.en: Build the prototype with the most capable model to establish a performance baseline.
rows.zh: 原文建议先用能力最强的模型构建原型，以建立性能基线。

rows.en: Then try replacing larger models with smaller ones where they still meet accuracy targets.
rows.zh: 在达到准确率目标后，再尝试用较小模型替换较大模型以优化成本和延迟。

rows.en: Evals are the mechanism that tells you where smaller models succeed or fail.
rows.zh: 评估体系是判断小模型是否足够的依据，而不是主观猜测。

sections.title: 工具决定 Agent 能做什么

rows.en: Agents need data tools, action tools, and orchestration tools.
rows.zh: Agent 通常需要数据工具、动作工具和编排工具三类能力。

rows.en: Each tool should have a standardized definition and be well documented, tested, and reusable.
rows.zh: 每个工具都应有标准化定义，并具备良好文档、测试和复用性。

rows.en: As the number of tools increases, consider splitting tasks across multiple agents.
rows.zh: 当工具数量增加时，可以考虑把任务拆给多个 Agent，但这不是默认起点。

sections.title: 指令把业务流程变成可执行步骤

rows.en: Use existing operating procedures, support scripts, or policy documents to create LLM-friendly routines.
rows.zh: 可以把现有 SOP、支持脚本或政策文档转化为适合 LLM 执行的流程。

rows.en: Make sure every step corresponds to a specific action or output.
rows.zh: 流程中的每一步都应对应明确行动或输出。

rows.en: A robust routine anticipates common variations and includes conditional branches.
rows.zh: 稳健流程会预判用户信息不完整、异常问题等边界情况，并写入条件分支。

sections.title: 默认先最大化单 Agent 能力

rows.en: A single agent can handle many tasks by incrementally adding tools.
rows.zh: 单 Agent 可以通过逐步添加工具处理许多任务。

rows.en: Every orchestration approach needs a run loop until an exit condition is reached.
rows.zh: 无论哪种编排方式，都需要运行循环，直到满足退出条件。

rows.en: Prompt templates can reduce maintenance without moving to a multi-agent framework.
rows.zh: 在不切换多 Agent 的情况下，提示词模板也能降低复杂度和维护成本。

rows.en: Use multiple agents when complex logic or tool overload prevents reliable execution.
rows.zh: 只有复杂逻辑或工具过载导致执行不稳定时，才应考虑多 Agent。

rows.en: The issue is not just the number of tools, but their similarity or overlap.
rows.zh: 工具问题不只在数量，也在相似性和重叠程度。

rows.en: If improving tool clarity does not improve performance, introduce more distinct agents.
rows.zh: 如果提升工具命名、参数和描述仍无改善，再引入职责更清晰的 Agent。

rows.en: The manager pattern uses a central agent to coordinate specialized agents via tool calls.
rows.zh: 管理者模式由中心 Agent 通过工具调用协调多个专业 Agent。

rows.en: The decentralized pattern lets agents hand off tasks to one another based on specialization.
rows.zh: 去中心化模式让多个 Agent 根据专长相互交接任务。

rows.en: Pick the pattern that matches who should control workflow execution and user access.
rows.zh: 选择模式时应看谁需要控制工作流，以及谁能直接接触用户。

sections.title: 护栏是生产路径的一部分

rows.en: Guardrails manage risks around data privacy, content safety, relevance, and tool use.
rows.zh: 护栏用于管理数据隐私、内容安全、相关性和工具使用风险。

rows.en: Risk ratings can pause high-risk functions or escalate to a human.
rows.zh: 工具风险评级可触发高风险函数暂停检查，或升级给人工处理。

rows.en: Guardrails should evolve from real-world edge cases and failures.
rows.zh: 护栏应根据真实边界情况和失败案例持续演进。

sections.title: 人工介入是可靠性机制

rows.en: Human intervention helps improve real-world performance without compromising user experience.
rows.zh: 人工介入能在不破坏用户体验的前提下提升真实表现。

rows.en: Escalate when the agent exceeds failure thresholds or attempts high-risk actions.
rows.zh: 当 Agent 超过失败阈值或执行高风险动作时，应升级给人工。

rows.en: For a coding agent, this means handing control back to the user.
rows.zh: 对于 coding agent，这意味着在无法完成或风险过高时把控制权交还给用户。

sections.title: 可靠 Agent 来自渐进扩展

rows.en: The path to successful deployment is not all-or-nothing.
rows.zh: 成功部署不是非黑即白的一次性选择。

rows.en: Start small, validate with real users, and grow capabilities over time.
rows.zh: 应从小处开始，与真实用户验证，并随时间逐步扩展能力。

rows.en: Agents can deliver business value by automating entire workflows with intelligence and adaptability.
rows.zh: 在正确基础和迭代方法下，Agent 可以以智能和适应性自动化完整工作流。

quiz.question: 哪一项最准确地区分 Agent 与普通 LLM 应用？
options: 是否由 LLM 控制工作流执行并动态使用工具
是否一定包含多个 Agent
quiz.explain: 原文明确排除了简单聊天机器人、单轮 LLM 和分类器，关键边界是 LLM 是否管理工作流执行并选择工具。
quiz.wrongReason: 其他选项要么是界面或模型规模问题，要么把多 Agent 当成必要条件，均不符合原文。

quiz.question: 在什么场景下更应该优先考虑 Agent？
options: 所有能接 API 的场景
需要复杂判断、规则难维护或依赖非结构化数据的场景
只需要固定表单校验的场景
成本最低的批处理任务
quiz.explain: 原文列出的三类高价值场景是复杂决策、难维护规则和非结构化数据。
quiz.wrongReason: 原文强调如果确定性方案足够，就不必构建 Agent。

quiz.question: OpenAI 指南推荐的模型选择顺序是什么？
options: 先选最便宜模型，再补护栏
先用强模型建立 eval 基线，再在可行处换小模型
每个任务都必须用同一个模型
直接用多 Agent 替代模型评估
quiz.explain: 原文建议先用最强模型建立性能基线，再在满足准确率后优化成本和延迟。
quiz.wrongReason: 这些说法都绕开了 eval baseline，是原文不支持的策略。

quiz.question: 什么时候更有理由拆成多 Agent？
options: 项目一开始就应该拆分
当复杂逻辑或工具重叠导致单 Agent 不稳定时
只要工具数量超过 3 个
为了让架构看起来更高级
quiz.explain: 原文建议先最大化单 Agent，只有复杂逻辑或工具过载无法通过清晰工具定义改善时再拆分。
quiz.wrongReason: 多 Agent 是复杂度管理手段，不是默认架构目标。

original.title: A practical guide to building agents

rows.en:
Large language models are becoming increasingly capable of handling complex, multi-step tasks. Advances in reasoning, multimodality, and tool use have unlocked a new category of LLM-powered systems known as agents.

This guide is designed for product and engineering teams exploring how to build their first agents, distilling insights from numerous customer deployments into practical and actionable best practices. It includes frameworks for identifying promising use cases, clear patterns for designing agent logic and orchestration, and best practices to ensure your agents run safely, predictably, and effectively.
rows.zh:
大语言模型正越来越擅长处理复杂的多步骤任务。推理、多模态和工具使用能力的进步，催生了一类由 LLM 驱动的新系统，即 Agent。

本指南面向正在探索如何构建首个 Agent 的产品与工程团队，将大量客户部署经验提炼为务实、可落地的最佳实践。内容涵盖识别高价值用例的框架、设计 Agent 逻辑与编排的清晰模式，以及确保 Agent 安全、可预测且高效运行的实践方法。

rows.en: A workflow is a sequence of steps that must be executed to meet the user's goal, whether that's resolving a customer service issue, booking a restaurant reservation, committing a code change, or generating a report.

rows.en:
Applications that integrate LLMs but don't use them to control workflow execution - think simple chatbots, single-turn LLMs, or sentiment classifiers - are not agents.

More concretely, an agent possesses core characteristics that allow it to act reliably and consistently on behalf of a user:

It leverages an LLM to manage workflow execution and make decisions. It recognizes when a workflow is complete and can proactively correct its actions if needed. In case of failure, it can halt execution and transfer control back to the user.

集成了 LLM 但不使用 LLM 控制工作流执行的应用并不是 Agent，例如简单聊天机器人、单轮 LLM 或情感分类器。

更具体地说，Agent 具备若干核心特征，使其能够可靠且一致地代表用户行动：

它利用 LLM 管理工作流执行并做出决策。它能识别工作流何时完成，并在需要时主动纠正自己的行动。失败时，它可以停止执行并把控制权交还给用户。

groups.group: When should you build an agent?

rows.en: Building agents requires rethinking how your systems make decisions and handle complexity. Unlike conventional automation, agents are uniquely suited to workflows where traditional deterministic and rule-based approaches fall short.
rows.zh: 构建 Agent 需要重新思考系统如何决策以及如何处理复杂性。不同于传统自动化，Agent 特别适合那些传统确定性方法和基于规则的方法难以胜任的工作流。
rows.html: Building agents requires rethinking how your systems make decisions and handle complexity. Unlike conventional automation, agents are uniquely suited to workflows where traditional deterministic and rule-based approaches fall short.
rows.zhHtml: 构建 Agent 需要重新思考系统如何决策以及如何处理复杂性。不同于传统自动化，Agent 特别适合那些传统确定性方法和基于规则的方法难以胜任的工作流。

rows.en: Consider the example of payment fraud analysis. A traditional rules engine works like a checklist, flagging transactions based on preset criteria. In contrast, an LLM agent functions more like a seasoned investigator, evaluating context, considering subtle patterns, and identifying suspicious activity even when clear-cut rules aren't violated. This nuanced reasoning capability is exactly what enables agents to manage complex, ambiguous situations effectively.
rows.zh: 以支付欺诈分析为例。传统规则引擎像清单一样，根据预设标准标记交易。相比之下，LLM Agent 更像经验丰富的调查员，会评估上下文、考虑细微模式，并在没有违反明确规则的情况下识别可疑活动。正是这种细致的推理能力，使 Agent 能够有效处理复杂而模糊的情境。

rows.en:
As you evaluate where agents can add value, prioritize workflows that have previously resisted automation, especially where traditional methods encounter friction:

**Complex decision-making** Workflows involving nuanced judgment, exceptions, or context-sensitive decisions, for example refund approval in customer service workflows.

**Difficult-to-maintain rules** Systems that have become unwieldy due to extensive and intricate rulesets, making updates costly or error-prone, for example performing vendor security reviews.

**Heavy reliance on unstructured data** Scenarios that involve interpreting natural language, extracting meaning from documents, or interacting with users conversationally, for example processing a home insurance claim.
rows.zh:
在评估 Agent 能在哪些场景创造价值时，应优先考虑过去难以自动化的工作流，尤其是传统方法存在明显摩擦的场景：

**复杂决策** 涉及细微判断、例外情况或上下文敏感决策的工作流，例如客服流程中的退款审批。

**难以维护的规则** 由于规则集庞大而复杂，系统变得笨重，导致更新成本高或容易出错，例如执行供应商安全审查。

**高度依赖非结构化数据** 需要解释自然语言、从文档中提取含义，或以对话方式与用户交互的场景，例如处理家庭保险理赔。

In its most fundamental form, an agent consists of three core components:

**Model** The LLM powering the agent's reasoning and decision-making.

**Tools** External functions or APIs the agent can use to take action.

**Instructions** Explicit guidelines and guardrails defining how the agent behaves.

From there, try swapping in smaller models to see if they still achieve acceptable results. This way, you don't prematurely limit the agent's abilities, and you can diagnose where smaller models succeed or fail.

In summary, the principles for choosing a model are simple:

Set up evals to establish a performance baseline.

rows.en:
High-quality instructions are essential for any LLM-powered app, but especially critical for agents. Clear instructions reduce ambiguity and improve agent decision-making, resulting in smoother workflow execution and fewer errors.

**Use existing documents** When creating routines, use existing operating procedures, support scripts, or policy documents to create LLM-friendly routines. In customer service for example, routines can roughly map to individual articles in your knowledge base.

**Prompt agents to break down tasks** Providing smaller, clearer steps from dense resources helps minimize ambiguity and helps the model better follow instructions.
rows.zh:
高质量指令对任何由 LLM 驱动的应用都很重要，对 Agent 尤其关键。清晰的指令能够减少歧义、改善 Agent 决策，从而让工作流执行更顺畅、错误更少。

**使用现有文档** 创建例程时，使用现有操作流程、支持脚本或政策文档来创建适合 LLM 的例程。例如在客服场景中，例程大致可以映射到知识库中的单篇文章。

**提示 Agent 拆解任务** 从密集资料中提供更小、更清晰的步骤，有助于减少歧义，并帮助模型更好地遵循指令。

rows.en:
**Define clear actions** Make sure every step in your routine corresponds to a specific action or output. For example, a step might instruct the agent to ask the user for their order number or to call an API to retrieve account details. Being explicit about the action (and even the wording of a user-facing message) leaves less room for errors in interpretation.

**Capture edge cases** Real-world interactions often create decision points such as how to proceed when a user provides incomplete information or asks an unexpected question. A robust routine anticipates common variations and includes instructions on how to handle them with conditional steps or branches such as an alternative step if a required piece of info is missing.
rows.zh:
**定义清晰行动** 确保例程中的每一步都对应具体行动或输出。例如，某个步骤可以指示 Agent 向用户询问订单号，或调用 API 获取账户详情。明确行动（甚至明确面向用户消息的措辞）可以减少解释错误的空间。

**覆盖边界情况** 真实交互常会产生决策点，例如用户提供的信息不完整或提出意外问题时该如何继续。稳健的例程会预判常见变化，并用条件步骤或分支说明如何处理，例如在缺少必要信息时采用替代步骤。

rows.en:
While it's tempting to immediately build a fully autonomous agent with complex architecture, customers typically achieve greater success with an incremental approach.

In general, orchestration patterns fall into two categories:

**Single-agent systems**, where a single model equipped with appropriate tools and instructions executes workflows in a loop.

**Multi-agent systems**, where workflow execution is distributed across multiple coordinated agents.
rows.zh:
尽管人们很容易想立即构建一个具备复杂架构的完全自主 Agent，但客户通常通过渐进式方法获得更大成功。

一般来说，编排模式分为两类：

**单 Agent 系统**，由一个配备适当工具和指令的模型在循环中执行工作流。

**多 Agent 系统**，工作流执行分布在多个协同 Agent 之间。

rows.en: An effective strategy for managing complexity without switching to a multi-agent framework is to use prompt templates. Rather than maintaining numerous individual prompts for distinct use cases, use a single flexible base prompt that accepts policy variables. This template approach adapts easily to various contexts, significantly simplifying maintenance and evaluation. As new use cases arise, you can update variables rather than rewriting entire workflows.

rows.en:
For many complex workflows, splitting up prompts and tools across multiple agents allows for improved performance and scalability. When your agents fail to follow complicated instructions or consistently select incorrect tools, you may need to further divide your system and introduce more distinct agents.

Practical guidelines for splitting agents include:

**Complex logic** When prompts contain many conditional statements (multiple if-then-else branches), and prompt templates get difficult to scale, consider dividing each logical segment across separate agents.
rows.zh:
对于许多复杂工作流，将提示词和工具拆分到多个 Agent 中，可以提升性能和可扩展性。当 Agent 无法遵循复杂指令，或持续选择错误工具时，可能需要进一步拆分系统，引入职责更清晰的 Agent。

拆分 Agent 的实用准则包括：

**复杂逻辑** 当提示词包含许多条件语句（多个 if-then-else 分支），且提示词模板变得难以扩展时，可以考虑把每个逻辑片段拆分到不同 Agent。

rows.en: **Tool overload** The issue isn't solely the number of tools, but their similarity or overlap. Some implementations successfully manage more than 15 well-defined, distinct tools while others struggle with fewer than 10 overlapping tools. Use multiple agents if improving tool clarity by providing descriptive names, clear parameters, and detailed descriptions doesn't improve performance.

rows.en:
While multi-agent systems can be designed in numerous ways for specific workflows and requirements, our experience with customers highlights two broadly applicable categories:

**Manager (agents as tools)** A central "manager" agent coordinates multiple specialized agents via tool calls, each handling a specific task or domain.

**Decentralized (agents handing off to agents)** Multiple agents operate as peers, handing off tasks to one another based on their specializations.

虽然多 Agent 系统可以针对特定工作流和需求设计成多种形式，但根据我们的客户经验，有两类模式具有广泛适用性：

**去中心化（Agent 向 Agent 交接）** 多个 Agent 以对等方式运行，并根据各自专长相互交接任务。

In the above example, the initial user message is sent to `triage_agent`. Recognizing that the input concerns a recent purchase, the `triage_agent` would invoke a handoff to the `order_management_agent`, transferring control to it.

This pattern is especially effective for scenarios like conversation triage, or whenever you prefer specialized agents to fully take over certain tasks without the original agent needing to remain involved. Optionally, you can equip the second agent with a handoff back to the original agent, allowing it to transfer control again if necessary.

rows.en: Well-designed guardrails help you manage data privacy risks (for example, preventing system prompt leaks) or reputational risks (for example, enforcing brand aligned model behavior). Guardrails are a critical component of any LLM-based deployment, but should be coupled with robust authentication and authorization protocols, strict access controls, and standard software security measures.

rows.code:
from agents import (
    Agent,
    GuardrailFunctionOutput,
    InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered,
    RunContextWrapper,
    Runner,
    TResponseInputItem,
    input_guardrail,
    Guardrail,
    GuardrailTripwireTriggered,
)
from pydantic import BaseModel


class ChurnDetectionOutput(BaseModel):
    is_churn_risk: bool
    reasoning: str


churn_detection_agent = Agent(
    name="Churn Detection Agent",
    instructions=(
        "Identify if the user message indicates a potential customer churn risk."
    ),
    output_type=ChurnDetectionOutput,
)


@input_guardrail
async def churn_detection_tripwire(
    ctx: RunContextWrapper[None],
    agent: Agent,
    input: str | list[TResponseInputItem],
) -> GuardrailFunctionOutput:
    result = await Runner.run(
        churn_detection_agent,
        input,
        context=ctx.context,
    )

    return GuardrailFunctionOutput(
        output_info=result.final_output,
        tripwire_triggered=result.final_output.is_churn_risk,
    )


customer_support_agent = Agent(
    name="Customer Support Agent",
    instructions=(
        "You are a customer support agent. You help customers with their questions."
    ),
    input_guardrails=[
        Guardrail(guardrail_function=churn_detection_tripwire),
    ],
)


async def main():
    # This should be ok
    await Runner.run(customer_support_agent, "Hello!")
    print("Hello message passed")

    # This should trip the guardrail
    try:
        await Runner.run(
            customer_support_agent,
            "I think I might cancel my subscription",
        )
        print("Guardrail didn't trip - this is unexpected")
    except GuardrailTripwireTriggered:
        print("Churn detection guardrail tripped")

rows.en: The Agents SDK treats guardrails as first-class concepts, relying on optimistic execution by default. Under this approach, the primary agent proactively generates outputs while guardrails run concurrently, triggering exceptions if constraints are breached.
rows.zh: Agents SDK 将护栏视为一等概念，并默认采用乐观执行。在这种方式下，主 Agent 会主动生成输出，同时护栏并发运行；如果约束被违反，则触发异常。

rows.en: Guardrails can be implemented as functions or agents that enforce policies such as jailbreak prevention, relevance validation, keyword filtering, blocklist enforcement, or safety classification. For example, the agent above processes a math question input optimistically until the `math_homework_tripwire` guardrail identifies a violation and raises an exception.

rows.en:
Human intervention is a critical safeguard enabling you to improve an agent's real-world performance without compromising user experience. It's especially important early in deployment, helping identify failures, uncover edge cases, and establish a robust evaluation cycle. Implementing a human intervention mechanism allows the agent to gracefully transfer control when it can't complete a task. In customer service, this means escalating the issue to a human agent. For a coding agent, this means handing control back to the user. Two primary triggers typically warrant human intervention:

**Exceeding failure thresholds:** Set limits on agent retries or actions. If the agent exceeds these limits (e.g., fails to understand customer intent after multiple attempts), escalate to human intervention.
rows.zh:
人工介入是一项关键防护措施，使你能够在不损害用户体验的情况下改进 Agent 的真实表现。它在部署早期尤其重要，有助于识别失败、发现边界情况，并建立稳健的评估循环。实现人工介入机制后，当 Agent 无法完成任务时，可以优雅地转移控制权。在客服场景中，这意味着将问题升级给人工客服。对于编码 Agent，这意味着把控制权交还给用户。通常有两个主要触发条件需要人工介入：

**超过失败阈值：** 为 Agent 重试次数或操作次数设置上限。如果 Agent 超过这些限制（例如多次尝试后仍无法理解客户意图），就升级到人工介入。

rows.en: **High-risk actions:** Actions that are sensitive, irreversible, or have high stakes should trigger human oversight until confidence in the agent's reliability grows. Examples include canceling user orders, authorizing large refunds, or making payments.

rows.en: Agents mark a new era in workflow automation, where systems can reason through ambiguity, take action across tools, and handle multi-step tasks with a high degree of autonomy. Unlike simpler LLM applications, agents execute workflows end-to-end, making them well-suited for use cases that involve complex decisions, unstructured data, or brittle rule-based systems.
rows.zh: Agent 标志着工作流自动化进入新阶段：系统能够在模糊情境中推理，跨工具采取行动，并以高度自主性处理多步骤任务。不同于更简单的 LLM 应用，Agent 可以端到端执行工作流，因此非常适合涉及复杂决策、非结构化数据或脆弱规则系统的用例。

rows.en: To build reliable agents, start with strong foundations: pair capable models with well-defined tools and clear, structured instructions. Use orchestration patterns that match your complexity level, starting with a single agent and evolving to multi-agent systems only when needed. Guardrails are critical at every stage, from input filtering and tool use to human-in-the-loop intervention, helping ensure agents operate safely and predictably in production.
rows.zh: 要构建可靠的 Agent，应从坚实基础开始：将能力合适的模型、定义清晰的工具，以及明确且结构化的指令结合起来。选择与复杂度匹配的编排模式，从单 Agent 起步，仅在需要时演进到多 Agent 系统。护栏在每个阶段都至关重要，从输入过滤、工具使用到人在回路介入，都能帮助确保 Agent 在生产环境中安全、可预测地运行。

rows.en: The path to successful deployment isn't all-or-nothing. Start small, validate with real users, and grow capabilities over time. With the right foundations and an iterative approach, agents can deliver real business value - automating not just tasks, but entire workflows with intelligence and adaptability.
rows.zh: 成功部署并不是非此即彼。先从小处开始，用真实用户验证，并随着时间逐步扩展能力。具备正确基础并采用迭代方法后，Agent 可以交付真实业务价值：不仅自动化任务，还能以智能性和适应性自动化整个工作流。
